tasks.short: Track regulatory and technology changes, assess their relevance, and agree changes to search marketing practice.

steps.what: Read regulatory publications and technology guidance, noting relevant changes.

loop.input: New publications from approved sources, with dates, jurisdiction and source links.
loop.output: Source notes containing changes, quoted passages, dates and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for each claim; distinguish proposals, enacted rules and effective dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per publication; unreadable or unsupported items enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feeds and keyword rules retrieve publications, but cannot reliably extract changes from varied prose.

steps.what: Discuss developments with colleagues and attend selected workshops or professional meetings.
Update the change register in {DOCS}, recording sources and follow-up dates.
Compare changes with current tracking, advertising and content practices.

loop.input: Reviewed changes, current marketing controls and campaign inventory.
loop.output: Draft impact assessment linking possible gaps to source passages and affected practices.
loop.check: Strategist checks factual mappings; uncertain legal interpretations are explicitly referred to the compliance lead.
loop.stop: One assessment and one revision per change; missing controls or conflicting sources require human assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applicability depends on the meaning of legal and technical prose and the actual marketing practice.

steps.what: Agree required actions, accountable roles and deadlines with marketing and compliance colleagues.
Send the approved action plan through {EMAIL} and request progress updates.

tasks.design: A scheduled flow in {WORKFLOW} collects approved publications from {GOV_PORTAL} and {DOCS}, removes duplicates and creates source-linked change notes through a bounded reading loop. A second bounded loop drafts impact assessments against documented marketing controls; people agree actions, while {WORKFLOW} maintains the register and sends reminders through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were scattered, applicability required reading, and maintaining a reliable register brought little immediate campaign benefit.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing feeds, document extraction and configurable records handle collection and tracking. Bounded text extraction can reduce reading time, while AI-assisted coding can make small source adapters cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Source coverage, changing effective dates and legal applicability still need specialist judgement. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national rules determine consultation requirements for changes affecting employees.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which change matters commercially, questioning a confident interpretation and learning through trusted professional relationships.

ambition.what: A source-linked marketing change clinic for campaign owners.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time maintaining reading lists and more time testing how changes affect campaigns. They can prioritise the clinic agenda; legal interpretation and control approval remain with the compliance lead.

reach.task: Prepare a briefing on how regulatory changes affect public claims.
reach.learn: Separate binding requirements from commentary and explain uncertainty without overstating it.

evidence.claim: Source collection, duplicate removal, dated registers and reminders can use deterministic automation.
Source-linked extraction can assist reading, but applicability assessment needs human judgement.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent citations, supporting explicit source checks for generated briefings.

assumptions: The initial scope covers a defined set of marketing practices, jurisdictions and approved sources.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a pilot, not measured delivery results or elapsed-time guarantees.
Consultation effort covers checking national rules and completing applicable consultation; substantial negotiation could extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which sources, jurisdictions and languages the team must cover.
Whether marketing controls and campaign inventories are documented and current.
Who approves legal interpretations and remediation priorities.
Which access permissions and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which authoritative sources provide stable feeds, version histories and effective-date metadata?
How accurately can extraction distinguish proposals from rules in force across the required languages?
new_work: Review extracted changes and resolve ambiguous applicability.
Maintain the source list and repair failed collection routes.
Keep marketing controls current and close completed actions.
Check a sample of summaries against original publications.
tasks.statement: Keep abreast of government regulations and emerging Web technology to ensure regulatory compliance by reviewing current literature, talking with colleagues, participating in educational programs, attending meetings or workshops, or participating in professional organizations or conferences.

tasks.short: Coordinate stock, listings and search campaigns to resolve customer-facing product availability problems.

steps.what: Read the customer-service case and identify the affected product and availability complaint.
Check sellable stock, reservations and replenishment information.
Compare shop availability and delivery claims with the stock snapshot.
Check which search campaigns send customers to the affected product.
Agree a remedy with customer service, operations and merchandising.
Correct the product listing or delivery message.
Pause or redirect affected search campaigns within the agreed remedy.
Explain the resolution to the customer and address remaining concerns.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins product identifiers and timestamped stock from the {OPS_SYSTEM} with listings in the {ECOMMERCE} and campaign destinations in the {ADS}. The {HELPDESK} receives a discrepancy bundle, and the {WORKFLOW} routes listing and campaign changes to their authorised owners. Customer service receives the confirmed remedy for its customer conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, shop listings, campaign destinations and customer cases use separate identifiers and update schedules. Staff bridge the gaps through messages and repeated screen checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins, freshness checks and configured approval actions cover the main preparation work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and discrepancy views.
tasks.still_hard: Sellable stock may differ from physical stock, and replenishment dates may be uncertain. Substitutions, customer promises and commercial priorities still require agreement.
tasks.human_edge: People decide whether to wait, substitute, redirect or stop promotion, and handle customers whose expectations cannot be met.

ambition.what: Intraday search-campaign availability review

tasks.altitude: The strategist reviews a short mismatch queue instead of tracing each complaint across screens. With delegated authority, they can approve temporary campaign pauses within agreed limits; operations retains stock and replenishment decisions.

reach.task: Prioritise product-feed and availability corrections.
reach.learn: Learn sellable-stock rules, reservation timing, product variants and shop-feed refresh behaviour.

evidence.claim: Product identifiers and timestamped stock allow deterministic comparison of availability across systems.
Listing and campaign changes can use configured approval actions where interfaces support them.
Resolving uncertain replenishment and customer promises remains a collaborative judgement task.

assumptions: This is a company that markets physical products through an online shop.
Customer service supplies a product identifier; incomplete cases enter an exception queue.
Time shares include the collaborating roles' contribution and are planning estimates.
Structured comparison offers more scope than the task's low overall gain prior suggests; remedy decisions stay human.
The integration excludes unnecessary customer personal data and does not introduce employee performance monitoring.
Configured write actions are available; unsupported interfaces would increase coding and integration time.
unknowns: Which system defines sellable stock and its freshness limit?
Do variants share stable identifiers across the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ECOMMERCE} and {ADS}?
Who can approve listing corrections and campaign pauses?
How often are reported shortages genuine rather than delayed updates?
Which access and consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Can stale data be distinguished from a true availability mismatch?
Which remedies can be represented as existing configured actions?
What checks prevent repeated pauses and restarts when stock fluctuates?
new_work: Resolve missing product identifiers and ambiguous variants.
Review listing and campaign change proposals.
Maintain stock definitions, freshness limits and destination mappings.
Monitor failed updates and confirm that applied remedies reached each system.
tasks.statement: Resolve product availability problems in collaboration with customer service staff.

tasks.short: Implement consistent online enquiry handling, service guidance and escalation processes.

steps.what: Review online enquiries, complaints and service metrics to identify recurring failures.

loop.input: A permitted, minimised ticket sample and an approved service issue taxonomy
loop.output: Issue labels and a summary linked to ticket references
loop.check: Validate labels against the taxonomy; review a sample and all uncertain or severe cases.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per batch; unresolved cases enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text descriptions express the same service failure in different ways; existing ticket fields may be incomplete.

steps.what: Agree response promises, handoffs and escalation ownership with the service team.
Draft service procedures, response templates and escalation guidance.

loop.input: Service process decisions, approved service facts and controlled document templates
loop.output: Procedure and response drafts with source references and explicit gaps
loop.check: Check promises, escalation ownership and factual claims against approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per document; missing policy decisions return to the service manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer-facing wording and explanations vary by issue; fixed fields alone do not produce clear guidance.

steps.what: Configure intake forms, routing, service timers and response templates in a test environment.
Trial customer journeys and check routing, accessibility and escalation behaviour.
Approve and publish the service process after resolving blocking defects.

tasks.design: Use existing forms, queues, timers and templates in the {HELPDESK}, connected to the {CMS}. Small bounded loops summarise permitted ticket samples and draft guidance from approved policy; configured workflows handle acknowledgements and routing. The service manager approves publication, and the {BI} tracks missed promises and repeat contacts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service promises and ownership were often unclear, while recurring problems were buried in ticket text. Teams maintained guidance separately from live queue settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing service configuration handles most execution. Bounded text classification and drafting reduce the cost of preparing changes and keeping guidance consistent.
tasks.still_hard: Staff capacity, unhappy customers and contested ownership remain human problems. GDPR limits ticket reuse; national rules may require employee consultation if individual service monitoring changes.
tasks.human_edge: Set realistic service promises, hear frustration and negotiate handoffs that teams can actually sustain.

ambition.what: After-hours enquiry intake with accurate acknowledgements and next-shift routing

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time diagnosing broken customer journeys and running service trials. They can propose and test process changes; customer service management retains authority over promises and release.

reach.task: Improve enquiry forms and service status messages
reach.learn: Accessible forms, error recovery and usability testing

reach.task: Align campaign promises with service capacity
reach.learn: Queue capacity, service commitments and campaign demand planning

evidence.claim: Configured queues, timers, acknowledgements and templates can implement repeatable service processes.
Free-text issue classification and policy-grounded drafting suit bounded loops; the digest supplies no direct case for this service redesign.

assumptions: Scope covers one online enquiry journey using an existing service system.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
This task implements service processes; it does not replace all customer conversations.
Existing service features are checked before adding code.
The access range includes consultation where national rules require it; a formal process may take longer.
The future loops assist internal preparation rather than autonomously resolve complaints.
unknowns: Which routing, testing and publication features are already available?
Who can approve customer promises and queue changes?
Can ticket samples be used for analysis under existing GDPR arrangements?
Would the change introduce individual employee monitoring or require consultation under national rules?
What service capacity exists outside normal working hours?
research_questions: Which enquiry journeys cause the most repeat contact or abandonment?
Do current ticket categories already provide enough detail without a model loop?
Can representatives complete the proposed process under realistic queue pressure?
Does acknowledgement wording accurately describe when a person will respond?
new_work: Review uncertain ticket labels and severe issues.
Approve wording and maintain source policies.
Resolve routing exceptions and monitor missed service promises.
Retest forms and templates after policy or queue changes.
Maintain ticket minimisation, access and retention controls.
tasks.statement: Implement online customer service processes to ensure positive and consistent user experiences.

tasks.short: Evaluate marketing technology, reuse existing capacity and procure approved tools.

steps.what: Define campaign requirements and acceptance criteria in the {DOCS}.
Check contracts and the {OTHER} IT asset register for reusable licences.
Compare supplier quotes and total costs in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: A fixed set of quotes, commercial terms and capability documents.
loop.output: Source-linked prices, units, limits, renewal terms and capability claims.
loop.check: Validate currency, billing period and mandatory fields; calculate totals with code and review uncertain terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unresolved terms block a complete comparison.
loop.why_not_simpler: Quotes express usage tiers, exclusions and renewal terms in inconsistent prose and tables.

steps.what: Test shortlisted tools in the {OTHER} evaluation environment.
Review security, data use and integration risks in the {DOCS}.
Agree the selected tool and approve the budget.
Enter the approved requisition in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Check policy and issue the purchase order through the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: A requirements form in the {WORKFLOW} checks available contracts and the {OTHER} IT asset register before starting a purchase. A bounded extractor builds a quote comparison, while deterministic code calculates costs; the strategist and IT reviewer test suitability and risk. Approved choices populate the {PROCUREMENT}, whose existing controls gate the external purchase order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Licence availability, commercial terms and purchasing records were disconnected. Tool suitability and data risks still required practical evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Code assistance makes small register adapters and comparison checks cheaper to build. Bounded extraction handles variable quote formats; existing purchasing controls handle approvals.
tasks.still_hard: Contract interpretation, real integration effort and supplier lock-in remain difficult. Low purchase frequency can make bespoke integrations uneconomic.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an impressive demonstration from a tool that fits the team's actual work, support capacity and risk tolerance.

ambition.what: Quarterly marketing licence reuse and retirement decisions.

tasks.altitude: Occasional purchases require less comparison paperwork, freeing time for hands-on evaluation and licence reviews. No purchasing authority changes unless explicitly delegated; budget and contract commitments retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Review the marketing technology portfolio for renewal or retirement.
reach.learn: Total ownership cost, adoption measures, switching cost and supplier exit planning.

evidence.claim: Quote extraction with deterministic cost calculation is a feasible pattern; the digest does not document marketing technology selection.
A vendor case documents reduced requisition review effort in procurement; it does not establish equivalent results for marketing purchases.

assumptions: Shares cover active evaluation and purchase coordination across the named roles, excluding supplier waiting time.
The starter kit uses approved quote files and register exports; live integration is worthwhile only if reused across purchases.
Trials use synthetic or approved data and do not publish campaigns or incur unapproved spending.
GDPR, EU AI Act obligations and national rules are assessed against the selected tool's actual intended use.
Access estimates include ordinary internal consultation; formal employee consultation or contract negotiation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether licence allocation and usage records are complete enough to establish reuse.
Which security, privacy, legal and budget approvals are mandatory.
Whether the selected tool changes employee monitoring and requires consultation under national rules.
Whether purchasing volume justifies live integration rather than file imports.
Which supplier quotes and contracts may be processed in the chosen environment.
research_questions: Which commercial fields drive most comparison errors across typical supplier quotes?
Can existing purchasing configuration accept an approved comparison without a custom requisition adapter?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous quote terms and maintain extraction checks.
Maintain licence mappings, cost assumptions and acceptance criteria.
Review failed policy checks and duplicate requisitions.
Reassess supplier data use, renewal terms and tool adoption.
tasks.statement: Identify, evaluate, or procure hardware or software for implementing online marketing campaigns.

tasks.short: Identify practical ways to connect web applications with finance and other business systems.

steps.what: Clarify the marketing use case, required data and business constraints with technical colleagues.
Read interface documentation and existing integration notes.

loop.input: Approved interface documentation and existing integration notes.
loop.output: Capability register covering endpoints, authentication, fields, limits and documented gaps.
loop.check: Require a source passage and version for every capability; flag undocumented assumptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per interface; missing documentation goes to the integration specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Constraints and prerequisites appear in prose outside machine-readable interface schemas.

steps.what: Check enabled interfaces, available fields and access restrictions in the finance system.
Compare existing connectors, direct interfaces and file transfers against the brief.
Discuss feasible options, failure handling and ownership with the technical team.
Write the recommendation, data mapping and unresolved implementation questions.
Approve the recommended method for implementation planning.

tasks.design: A reusable capability register on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines interface documentation from the {DOCS} with authorised read-only configuration checks on the {ERP} and the relevant web system, such as the {CMS} or {ECOMMERCE}. A bounded extraction loop fills prose-based constraints, while deterministic rules compare verified options and generate the recommendation in the {DOCS}. A solution architect approves the method before implementation planning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documentation is scattered and may describe capabilities that are not enabled locally. Comparison work is repeated because verified profiles and ownership notes are rarely kept together.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine-readable schemas, read-only probes and reusable comparison rules handle much of the research. AI-assisted coding reduces adapter effort, and a bounded loop extracts constraints from prose.
tasks.still_hard: Access, undocumented customisations, data meaning and operational ownership need local expertise. GDPR and the EU AI Act must be assessed where relevant to the proposed data flow; this research task does not establish compliance.
tasks.human_edge: The strategist defines the marketing outcome and acceptable delay. Technical colleagues judge maintainability, security and responsibility when the connection fails.

ambition.what: Integration feasibility brief for proposed marketing experiments

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time hunting interface details and can bring technical colleagues a verified option matrix earlier. They gain clearer scope for proposing data connections; architecture approval remains with the solution architect.

reach.task: Specify data requirements and failure states for a connected customer journey.
reach.learn: Learn interface contracts, refresh delays, data mapping and behaviour when upstream systems fail.

evidence.claim: Schema comparison, capability checks and option-matrix generation can use deterministic code.
A bounded extraction loop can identify documented constraints while preserving source references.
Available interfaces do not settle architecture, data meaning or operational ownership.

assumptions: The strategist identifies methods with technical colleagues rather than approving production architecture alone.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The build creates a research and recommendation workspace, not the proposed production integrations.
The research-heavy prior supports substantial preparation savings; the low rule-coverage prior keeps method selection human.
Recommendation templates can be populated from structured decisions without generated prose.
Consultation requirements depend on the proposed data flow and national rules.
unknowns: Which web applications and business systems must connect?
Which interfaces are licensed, enabled and documented?
Are read-only metadata access and a test environment available?
What freshness, security and ownership requirements must each option satisfy?
Who approves architecture and any personal-data processing?
research_questions: Which capability checks can use schemas before prose extraction is needed?
Can verified profiles be reused across several marketing use cases?
Which unknowns materially change the preferred integration method?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and unsupported capability claims.
Refresh profiles when interface versions or configurations change.
Maintain connector eligibility rules and recommendation templates.
Investigate failed probes and refer unresolved architecture questions to technical owners.
tasks.statement: Identify methods for interfacing Web application technologies with enterprise resource planning or other system software.

tasks.short: Turn market and search evidence into product requirements with design and engineering.

steps.what: Review search, conversion and customer trends in the {BI}.
Read market research and customer feedback in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved market research, customer feedback and performance snapshot.
loop.output: Evidence notes linking needs, contradictory findings and gaps to source passages.
loop.check: Validate source references; strategist checks consequential findings and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document; unreadable sources return to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text research expresses needs and qualifications that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Agree user problems, feasibility constraints and priorities with design and engineering.
Write requirements and acceptance criteria in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Agreed priorities, cited evidence, constraints and a requirements template.
loop.output: Requirements draft with measurable acceptance criteria and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required sections and evidence links; strategist verifies intent and testability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision against review comments; unresolved trade-offs remain marked.
loop.why_not_simpler: Translating varied user needs into clear requirements requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Approve requirements and resolve scope trade-offs.
Transfer approved requirements and evidence links into the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure a reusable evidence view in the {BI}; bounded loops turn approved material in the {DOCS} into cited evidence notes and a requirements draft. People settle priorities and approve scope, after which a deterministic integration creates linked records in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, research language varied, and copying approved requirements between systems needed custom glue.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and document interfaces support a small reusable workflow. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation work; bounded extraction and drafting reduce document preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Search demand does not prove a product need. Sparse research, conflicting stakeholder goals and engineering uncertainty still require investigation and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Connect market evidence to a worthwhile user problem and negotiate a feasible scope without disguising uncertainty.

ambition.what: A pre-build search-demand assessment for proposed product features.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time testing product hypotheses with design and engineering. They can recommend evidence-backed acceptance criteria; product scope and funding remain with the product manager.

reach.task: Translate a user problem into a testable interaction requirement.
reach.learn: User flows, accessibility requirements and prototype evaluation.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Plan research that distinguishes expressed interest from an unmet need.
reach.learn: Sampling, interview design and limits of inference.

evidence.claim: Configured dashboards and deterministic record creation can handle structured evidence preparation and backlog transfer.
Bounded extraction and drafting can prepare requirements; source validation and human scope decisions remain necessary.

assumptions: This is occasional product discovery work within a larger marketing role.
A product manager has final scope authority.
The initial build uses aggregate data and approved research, with manual file import where connectors are unavailable.
Build ranges cover one reusable workflow and a small pilot, not a research repository migration.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; national rules govern any employee consultation required by the actual deployment.
unknowns: Which research and performance sources are available and reliable?
Can existing access permissions be preserved during extraction?
Who can approve requirements and create delivery records?
Does the proposed data use require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can reviewers trace every consequential requirement to evidence or an explicitly labelled hypothesis?
Does the existing {PROJECT} already support approved document-to-backlog transfer?
new_work: Review extracted findings and draft acceptance criteria.
Resolve missing evidence and conflicting research.
Maintain document templates, source permissions and backlog field mappings.
Check whether implemented features answer the original user problem.
tasks.statement: Define product requirements, based on market research analysis, in collaboration with user interface design and engineering staff.

tasks.short: Evaluate marketing suppliers and support negotiation of vendor or partner contracts.

steps.what: Gather supplier proposals, contract versions and service history from the {EMAIL}.
Compare fees, commitments and service metrics in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review scope, termination, measurement and data clauses in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Versioned contract draft, approved playbook and commercial comparison.
loop.output: Cited clause table, missing provisions and possible deviations requiring review.
loop.check: Verify quotations and locations; strategist checks service terms and refers legal issues to legal counsel.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguous or missing clauses remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Equivalent obligations appear in varied language and cross-referenced clauses.

steps.what: Agree negotiating priorities and concession limits.
Discuss service commitments and concessions with the supplier.
Document the recommendation, concessions and unresolved issues in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Verified negotiation notes, clause issues and calculated commercial comparison.
loop.output: Recommendation draft separating agreed points, proposed concessions and unresolved issues.
loop.check: Match amounts to calculations and commitments to notes; strategist verifies the recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported commitments are omitted and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiation notes need contextual synthesis into a concise recommendation.

steps.what: Approve the commercial recommendation or request further negotiation.

tasks.design: Configure an intake folder in the {DOCS} from selected {EMAIL} threads, then calculate commercial comparisons from verified structured fields. Bounded loops prepare cited clause issues and recommendations; people set the mandate, negotiate and approve the commercial decision, with approved records stored in the {CLM} where available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier terms arrived as inconsistent documents, versions were hard to track, and bespoke comparison tools were expensive for occasional use.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce reviewable clause tables, while inexpensive deterministic tools handle calculations and version checks. A small reusable pack can start from files without replacing procurement systems.
tasks.still_hard: Legal interpretation, bargaining power, hidden dependencies and supplier credibility remain difficult. Scanned documents, complex fee schedules and conflicting versions can erase preparation savings.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the supplier relationship, trade concessions deliberately and recognize commitments that need legal or commercial escalation.

ambition.what: A marketing-supplier measurement-terms review before commercial approval.

tasks.altitude: The strategist brings a clearer view of measurement rights, service commitments and total cost to negotiations. They gain influence over service acceptance criteria; contract signature and legal approval remain with authorized roles.

reach.task: Assess the commercial value and measurement obligations of a marketing supplier.
reach.learn: Total-cost scenarios, service acceptance criteria and negotiation preparation.

evidence.claim: Structured fee comparisons and version checks are deterministic; clause extraction needs review against source text.
The digest documents automated procurement negotiation, but does not establish suitability for bespoke marketing contracts.

assumptions: The strategist supports procurement rather than holding contract-signing authority.
Legal review is a separate dependency and is not replaced by clause extraction.
Negotiation conversations stay within the approved mandate; binding commitments follow the existing signature process.
Commercial calculations use verified structured fields; extracted amounts require confirmation before calculation.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Confidential documents use approved processing arrangements and existing access restrictions.
The access range includes consultation under national rules if the actual deployment requires it.
unknowns: Which contract playbook and concession limits are approved?
Is a {CLM} available, or are contracts held in the {DOCS}?
Who provides legal review and commercial approval?
Can confidential supplier documents be processed in the proposed environment?
Are contract versions and commercial assumptions reliably identified?
research_questions: Which clause types can be extracted reliably from representative supplier contracts?
Can existing {CLM} configuration cover intake, comparisons and approval records?
What minimum review is needed to prevent an omitted clause from appearing acceptable?
new_work: Verify extracted clauses, fee fields and document versions.
Maintain the approved playbook and commercial comparison rules.
Escalate ambiguous terms and unsupported commitments.
Record final negotiated changes against the reviewed version.
tasks.statement: Assist in the evaluation or negotiation of contracts with vendors or online partners.

tasks.short: Develop and present evidence-backed campaign proposals for marketing investment decisions.

steps.what: Gather objectives, prior results, market opportunities and delivery constraints.
Estimate channel costs, conversion ranges and commercial scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss campaign concepts and choose a recommended audience, offer and channel mix.
Write the proposal with alternatives, economics, evidence, risks and a measurement plan.

loop.input: Selected concept, calculated scenarios, evidence pack and proposal template.
loop.output: A campaign proposal with referenced claims, alternatives and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Validate figures against scenario outputs and references against the evidence pack; strategist reviews the argument.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence remains marked as a gap and blocks unsupported claims.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but explaining the campaign's specific rationale requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Present the recommendation, answer challenges and negotiate scope.
Approve, reject or return the proposal within delegated investment authority.
Record the decision and hand approved scope to campaign delivery.

tasks.design: A proposal workspace in {PROJECT} assembles approved evidence from {BI} and {DOCS}, while a deterministic calculator produces scenarios from explicit assumptions. A bounded drafting loop fills the proposal in {DOCS}; the strategist chooses the concept and presents the recommendation. The marketing manager records the investment decision, and a configured workflow hands only approved scope to delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence gathering, scenario updates and repeated proposal writing consumed preparation time. Agreement on priorities and investment could not be reduced to a template.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable scenario calculators and evidence retrieval remove repeated assembly. Bounded drafting can turn a selected concept and verified numbers into a reviewable proposal.
tasks.still_hard: Forecasts depend on assumptions, channel overlap and delivery capacity. Executive persuasion and resolving conflicting objectives remain human work, so near-total automation is unlikely.
tasks.human_edge: Make an argument that reflects commercial priorities, defend its assumptions and change the recommendation when challenged.

ambition.what: A monthly comparison of a smaller pilot against the full campaign investment.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less of the week assembling proposals and more time testing assumptions with stakeholders. They can gain authority to recommend staged investment and stop criteria; final investment approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Compare campaign investments across competing commercial priorities.
reach.learn: Contribution economics, portfolio trade-offs and investment governance.

reach.task: Develop a campaign narrative from a commercial brief.
reach.learn: Audience framing, narrative structure and evidence-based persuasion.

evidence.claim: Scenario calculations and evidence-pack assembly can be deterministic; drafting can use a bounded loop over approved inputs.
The supplied digest does not document automated campaign proposal approval or establish that executive persuasion can be automated.

assumptions: Objectives, past results and approved assumptions exist in accessible records.
A proposal decision does not itself publish a campaign, transfer audience data or activate spend.
Rejected and returned proposals produce a decision record but no approved campaign proposal.
Build ranges cover one proposal template and scenario model; they are planning estimates.
Access work includes confidentiality, GDPR and EU AI Act applicability checks, plus national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Which commercial outcomes and cost assumptions govern investment decisions?
Who holds approval authority at each investment level?
Which proposal sections require specialist review?
How complete and comparable are historical campaign results?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the implementation?
research_questions: Which scenario presentation best communicates uncertainty without implying forecast precision?
How should staged campaign proposals account for learning value as well as immediate return?
new_work: Maintain scenario formulas, assumptions and proposal templates.
Review generated claims, references and the recommendation's logic.
Record approval scope and conditions precisely.
Compare forecasts with outcomes and update planning assumptions.
tasks.statement: Propose online or multiple-sales-channel campaigns to marketing executives.

tasks.short: Help develop transaction and security policies for search marketing and online purchases.

steps.what: Read existing policies, approved templates and relevant requirements.

loop.input: Approved policies, templates and requirements.
loop.output: Source register with relevant passages, dates and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Every passage links to its source; missing dates and conflicting requirements remain flagged.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting sources go to the policy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant obligations and scope appear in free text with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Check transaction settings and document how marketing data enters the purchase journey.
Discuss gaps, customer friction and acceptable controls with security and privacy specialists.
Draft policy changes and explain their effects on marketing and customer journeys.

loop.input: Agreed changes, approved source passages and policy template.
loop.output: Policy draft with change notes and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require source references for obligations; compare clauses against agreed changes and flag unsupported additions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved legal or security questions go to specialists.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations and policy wording depend on the particular customer journey and agreed trade-offs.

steps.what: Review the draft and authorise the policy version for release.
Publish the approved version and archive the superseded policy.

tasks.design: A reusable policy workspace in the {DOCS} combines approved templates with a source register and a read-only control inventory from the {ECOMMERCE}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare changes; specialists settle disputed requirements, and the policy owner authorises release through the {WORKFLOW}. Existing version controls publish and archive approved documents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies mix free text, technical settings and risk decisions. Templates help, but someone still has to trace sources and reconcile conflicting requirements.

tasks.short: Improve website and shopping-cart conversion through measured experiments against agreed business and customer guardrails.

steps.what: Choose an experiment and specify metrics, audience, guardrails and stopping rules.

Interpret results and recommend rollout, revision or rejection.

tasks.design: Configured dashboards in {BI} and an experimentation system in {OTHER} use validated conversion and order data, with deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded loop groups redacted feedback into hypotheses, while people choose experiments and review configured variants in {CMS} or {ECOMMERCE}. Deterministic QA and predefined statistical rules support manager-approved launches and releases, with automatic guardrail stops within the approved experiment limits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tracking and order data disagree, experiments need scarce design capacity, and low traffic makes results uncertain. Repeated manual reconciliation delays learning.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes validation jobs and automated checks cheaper. Existing experiment configuration handles assignment and analysis, while a bounded loop reduces feedback-reading effort.
tasks.still_hard: Automation cannot create statistical power or establish causality from observational funnels. Checkout restrictions, consent-related missing data and long-term customer effects remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a meaningful customer problem and reject conversion gains that damage clarity, trust, accessibility or commercial quality.

steps.what: Inspect existing listings and placement options in {PARTNER_PORTAL}.

tasks.design: A listing register in {WORKFLOW} combines authorised data from {PARTNER_PORTAL}, the location master and performance data in {BI}; deterministic comparisons prepare the shortlist and purchase request in {PROCUREMENT}. People negotiate and approve spend, then review the exact submission before an integration purchases the placement; verification results support invoice matching in {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Listing providers used different fields and access methods, while low purchase volumes rarely justified bespoke integrations.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable field mappings, existing approval flows and faster adapter development make a limited provider set practical. Comparison and submission do not require a model when inputs are structured.
tasks.still_hard: Provider access, location ownership verification, nonstandard terms and uncertain incremental value remain difficult. GDPR applies where listings contain personal contact details; contractual commitments need clear authority.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating concessions, judging provider credibility and deciding whether a placement deserves budget despite imperfect attribution.
